dedupe_keys.name: washington dc building energy benchmarking and beps performance disclosure

description: The District of Columbia publishes two building energy tables on Open Data DC under CC BY 4.0. Building Energy Benchmarks discloses the ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager results that owners of private buildings over 50,000 gross square feet, including multifamily buildings, and public buildings must report each year under the Clean and Affordable Energy Act of 2008: about 35,500 building-year rows with reporting year and status, owner and address, ward, year built, property type, floor area, ENERGY STAR score, site and source energy use intensity (also weather-normalised), total and per-fuel energy use including district chilled water, hot water and steam, monthly electricity and natural gas, greenhouse gas emissions, water use and enforcement action. Building Energy Performance Data discloses performance against the Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) created by the Clean Energy DC Omnibus Act of 2018, set no lower than the local median ENERGY STAR score by property type and first established on 1 January 2021 for six-year periods: 1,963 buildings with the applicable standard and metric, the building's metric, estimated distance from the standard, whether it meets it, and the approved compliance pathway. Coverage: Washington, DC, geolocated by the Master Address Repository. Access: free download and ArcGIS feature services. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: data are self-reported through Portfolio Manager, and only covered buildings above the size thresholds appear. Simulation uses: calibrating city building stock models, testing performance standard scenarios and retrofit targeting. Related records: ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager and the NYC and Seattle benchmarking datasets.
